download
                      (Optional) Specifies whether to automatically download patches from My Oracle Support
                      during Create Home, Deploy, or Patching modes.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      This parameter specifies whether to automatically download patches from My Oracle Support.
                      The default is YES. You use this option when you are using AutoUpgrade to patch an existing
                      database, and you can also use this option in the Create Home and Deploy modes to patch
                      target release database binaries before proceeding with a database upgrade.
                      When set to YES, you must either load My Oracle Support (MOS) credentials or an OAUTH
                      token into AutoUpgrade at the command line using the -load_password command-line option.

                      To perform a download, the following endpoints or URLs must be reachable for the specified
                      options:
                      My Oracle Support:
                      •     https://login-ext.identity.oraclecloud.com
                      •     https://updates.oracle.com
                      •     https://aru-akam.oracle.com
                      Latest AutoUpgrade:
                      •     https://edelivery.oracle.com
                      Oracle Update Advisor (OUA):
                      •     https://transport.oracle.com
                      •     https://objectstorage.us-ashburn-1.oraclecloud.com
                      The items downloaded are placed into the directory folder specified by the download_folder
                      parameter.
                      If proxy information is required to connect to My Oracle Support, then set proxy values using
                      the Linux operating system environment variables https_proxy, http_proxy, and no_proxy.

                      The supported format of the proxy definition is as follows, where user_info is a user account,
                      site is a URL, and port is a designated port for the proxy listener:

                      [https|http|socks5|socks]://(user_info@)site:port

                      (Optional) Specifies that AutoUpgrade gathers fixed object statistics on the source database
                      before starting the upgrade.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      Before an upgrade, Oracle recommends that you regather fixed object statistics.
                      Fixed objects are the X$ tables and their indexes. V$ performance views are defined through X$
                      tables. Gathering fixed object statistics is valuable for database performance, because these
                      statistics help the optimizer generate good execution plans, which can improve database
                      performance. Failing to obtain representative statistics can lead to suboptimal execution plans,
                      which can cause significant performance problems.

                      Options
                      [yes | no]

                      global.fixed_stats_before=yes


                      sales.fixed_stats_before=yes

                      Options
                      Earlier releases of AutoUpgrade required you to set target_home and target_version. In later
                      releases of AutoUpgrade, this restriction has been lifted for both Analyze and Fixups modes.
                      However, if you don't set target_home, then you must specify target_version. Either one of

                      When used with the AutoUpgrade command-line -patch option, you can define the target
                      home using the release version as a variable, so that the version number is included in the
                      directory file path when creating a new Oracle home. This can be useful if you are requesting
                      the latest version of release updates, because you do not have to find out what the latest
                      release update is to specify an Oracle home directory that includes that release update version
                      in the directory path. The syntax is as follows:

                      •     %RELEASE%: Major release number, For example: 19, 21, 26.
                      •     %UPDATE%: Release update. When the version is at least 23.26.0, the value of %UPDATE%
                            matches the numbers in the second and third positions of version, including the period. For
                            example, when the version is 23.26.1.0.0, then %UPDATE% corresponds to 26.1 when the
                            version is 23.26.1.0.0). For earlier release versions, %UPDATE% corresponds to the number
                            in the second position. For example, if the version is 19.30.0.0.0, then %UPDATE%
                            corresponds to 30.
                      •     %V1D%, %V2D%, %V3D%, %V4D%, or %V5D%: Release numbering where the %Vnumeral%
                            designation matches the number at the specified position in the target version.

                      Example
                      In the following examples, the path for the database is specified.


                      sales3.target_home=/U01/app/oracle/product/19.0.0/dbhome_1
                      sales1.target_home=/U01/app/oracle/product/23.0.0/dbhome_1


                      With the AutoUpgrade command-line option -patch, you can use the target home release path
                      variables to specify the patch information for the target home. Suppose AutoUpgrade installs
                      23.26.1 as the latest patch. You can include that patch number in the new target home path
                      using this syntax:
                      upg1.target_home=/u01/app/home/databases/%RELEASE%.%UPDATE%/home_1

                      The result is as follows:
                      /u01/app/home/databases/23.26.1/home_1

                      Suppose you are running AutoUpgrade with the -patch option for an Oracle Database 19c
                      release, and the patch is 19.30. The result then is as follows:
                      /u01/app/home/databases/19.30/home_1

                      Suppose you are running AutoUpgrade with the patch option for Oracle Database, and you
                      specify the full release numbering in the target home path using this syntax:
                      upg1.target_home=/u01/app/oracle/home/databases/%V1D%.%V2D%.%V3D%.%V4D%.%V5D%

                      The result then includes the full release numbering for the patch. For example:
                      /u01/app/oracle/home/databases/23.26.1.0.2

                      /01/app/oracle/home/databases/19.28.3.0.1

                      Because the numeric variables can be used in any sequence, you have complete control over

                      upg1.target_home=/u01/app/oracle/home/databases/%V1D%.%V4D%.%V5D% = /u01/app/
                      oracle//home/databases/23.1.0
                      upg1.target_home=/u01/app/oracle/home/databases/%V1D%.%V4D% = /u01/app/oracle//
                      home/databases/23.1
                      upg1.target_home=/u01/app/oracle/home/databases/%V5D% = /u01/app/oracle//home/
                      databases/0

                      (Optional) Generates a Guaranteed Restore Point (GRP) for database restoration.

                      If left at default value (yes), a fast recovery area configuration is required to create a GRP. If

                      and Standard Edition 2 databases, which do not support the Oracle Flashback technology
                      feature Flashback Database. If you do not specify the parameter, then the default value (yes) is

                      (Optional) Specifies the location of a Microsoft Windows credential object file that you have
                      previously generated with the AutoUpgrade command-line parameter load_win_credential.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      The purpose of this parameter is to create a credentials file to store the user and password
                      credentials for the owner of the Oracle Database binaries, and to specify the location of the
                      Administrator PowerShell credential object for those credentials, so that AutoUpgrade can be
                      run using that credential object during the Oracle Database upgrade. This parameter either can
                      be set globally, or you can modify it locally in the configuration file. To use this feature, you
                      must have already created the Windows PowerShell credential object, and then specify that
                      credential object in the configuration file using wincredential.

                      Use case:
                      You want to specify credentials for the owner of database binaries on a Microsoft Windows
                      server. To specify these credentials, after you enter the wincredential parameter in your
                      configuration file, you run AutoUpgrade in Configuration mode using the
                      load_win_credentials command-line parameter, and provide credentials as prompted.
                      Microsoft Windows Powershell then creates the credential object, and stores the generated
                      credential object in the path location you specify with wincredential. For example, in the
                      following file, the location of the credential file is specified with
                      upg1.wincredential=C:\Users\oracle\cred


                                Note
                                All services and auxiliary services are created automatically using ORADIM.


                      Examples
                      You can set the parameter globally, and modify it locally. For example:

                      global.autoupg_log_dir=C:\Users\oracle\autoupg
                      global.wincredential=C:\Users\oracle\globalcred

                      upg1.sid=db12201
                      upg1.source_home=C:\databases\ee\product\12.2\dbhome_1
                      upg1.upgrade_node=localhost
                      upg1.target_home=C:\databases\ee\product\18x\dbhome_1
                      upg1.target_base=C:\databases

                      With this configuration file example, the jobs for the database with the system identifier (SID)
                      db12201 will use the global credential C:\Users\oracle\globalcred\current_jobs.xml.
                      Because the credential C:\Users\oracle\localcred is set locally for all jobs specified with the
                      prefix upg2, the job for the database with SID db18x will use C:\Users\oracle\localcred.

                      Suppose you have a local job where you want to use another method for providing credentials,
                      but you also want to use global credentials for other jobs where you want to provide a global
                      credential. In that case, you can set the global credential for all jobs, but override that global
                      credential locally for the database where you do not want to provide a credential.
                      In the following example, the job specified with the prefix upg1 has the wincredential
                      parameter set to no (upg1.wincredential=NO). As a result the job specified with the upg1
                      prefix will fall back to a legacy service management method:

                      global.autoupg_log_dir=C:\Users\oracle\autoupg
                      global.wincredential=C:\Users\oracle\globalcred

                      upg1.sid=db12201
                      upg1.source_home=C:\databases\ee\product\12.2\dbhome_1
                      upg1.upgrade_node=localhost
                      upg1.target_home=C:\databases\ee\product\18x\dbhome_1
                      upg1.target_base=C:\databases
                      upg1.target_version=18.8.0.0

                      upg2.sid=db18x
                      upg2.source_home=C:\databases\ee\product\18x\dbhome_1
                      upg2.target_home=C:\databases\ee\product\19x\dbhome_1
                      upg2.wincredential=NO

                      As a result, The job for db12201 will use the global credential,
                      C:\Users\oracle\globalcred\current_jobs.xml. However, because the job identified with
                      the prefix upg2 is modified locally (upg2.wincredential=NO), the job for db18x will not use any
                      credential, but instead fall back to a legacy credential option. Also, as a result of this local
                      modification, the db18x job can use the drop_win_src_service configuration parameter, which
                      is otherwise not allowed if you specify a Windows credential in the configuration file.


Local Common Parameters for the AutoUpgrade Config File
                      The common Local parameters enable you to configure AutoUpgrade processing in the
                      configuration file (config) for specific Oracle Databases either for software maintenance (-
                      patch) or upgrade (upgrade).

                      •     after_action
                            (Optional) In deploy mode, specifies a custom action that you want to have performed
                            after completing the upgrade deploy job for the database identified by the prefix address.
                      •     before_action
                            (Optional) In deploy mode, specifies a custom action that you want to have performed
                            before starting the upgrade job for the specific database job addressed by the prefix.

after_action
                      (Optional) In deploy mode, specifies a custom action that you want to have performed after
                      completing the upgrade deploy job for the database identified by the prefix address.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      The script that you use must be in the form of name.ext (for example, myscript.sh, so that
                      AutoUpgrade can identify the type of script that you want to run.
                      Permitted extension options:
                      •     Unix shell (.sh)
                      •     Microsoft Windows batch (.bat, .cmd)
                      •     Microsoft Windows PowerShell (.ps1)
                      •     Oracle SQL file (.sql), with a local operation only designated by the prefix.


                                Note
                                The after_action.deploy and after_action.create_home parameters for
                                AutoUpgrade patching and the local parameter after_action cannot be specified in
                                the same configuration file.


                      By default, if the script fails, then AutoUpgrade continues to run. Use the Y flag to specify that
                      AutoUpgrade stops if the operating system detects that your script fails. If the script finishes
                      with a status different than 0, then it is considered a failed completion.

                      In contrast to the global after_action parameter, the local after_action parameter can
                      specify a SQL script, which then runs on the database using the target Oracle Database
                      binaries on a non-CDB Oracle home, or on CDB$ROOT. If you want to run additional container-

                      The output of the script is captured and stored in files. Both stdout and stderr are captured.
                      The files are stored in the postupgrade subdirectory in the directory matching the specific

                      The following environment variables are set in the shell that runs the script:

                      AutoUpgrade if the script fails:

                      to run if the script fails:

                      sales3.after_action=/user/path/script.sh

checklist
                      (Optional) Specifies the path to a checklist that you can use to override the default list of fixups
                      that AutoUpgrade performs, such as fixups that you do not want implemented automatically,
                      due to policy or security concerns.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      To use this parameter during other AutoUpgrade modes, you must run AutoUpgrade in
                      analyze mode. After AutoUpgrade finishes the analysis, you can then find the checklist file
                      identified by the database name under the precheck directory (dbname_checklist.cfg).
                      Update the file manually to exclude the fixups that you want AutoUpgrade to bypass, and save
                      the file with a new name. When you run AutoUpgrade again, you can specify the parameter
                      pointing to the checklist file that you created, and modify fixups that are performed for
                      individual databases. If you do not specify a checklist file path, then the set of fixups that run
                      during the upgrade is the latest version of the checklist file that is created during the deploy
                      mode that you specified.

                      Examples

                      sales.checklist=/u01/app/oracle/upgrade-jobs/salesdb_checklist.cfg


                      In the preceding example, salesdb_checklist.cfg is the checklist configuration file for the
                      database salesdb.

create_listener
                      (Optional) Creates a listener in the new Oracle home after an upgrade.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      During Deploy mode, AutoUpgrade can create a listener in the new (target) Oracle home.
                      There are four options:
                      •     (Default) Create a new listener named LISTENER on port 1521.
                      •     Specify both a custom listener name and port number. (For example: my_listener:49152)
                      •     Create multiple listeners by providing a comma-delimited list of listener names and ports.
                            (For example:
                            listener_name1:listener_port1,listener_name2:listener_port2, . . .).
                      •     Provide the path to a response file to configure the listener settings, such as a response
                            file generated by NETCA. (For example: /path/to/responsefile.rsp)


Database Upgrade Guide
E96252-82                                                                                                            August 11, 2026
Copyright © 1996, 2026, Oracle and/or its affiliates.                                                                 Page 78 of 245
                                                                                                                           Chapter 3
                                                        Common Parameters for the AutoUpgrade Configuration File (Upgrade and Patch)


                      Use this parameter if you want to create a listener in the new Oracle home, particularly if you
                      want to create a listener based on specific requirements.


                                Note
                                Listeners must have unique names. To avoid conflicts during migration from the earlier
                                release Oracle home to the new release Oracle home, and you use this parameter
                                option, then you have an existing listener in your current Oracle home, then you must
                                create a unique listener name.


                      Other AutoUpgrade modes can validate create_listener configuration choices, but the actual
                      creation of listeners only happens during Deploy mode, during the Postupgrade stage. After
                      the listener is created, AutoUpgrade automatically starts the listener. If an error occurs,
                      AutoUpgrade will continue to complete the upgrade job without interruption, but log a warning
                      message that provides information about why the listener creation process failed. This ensures
                      a seamless upgrade experience while maintaining visibility into any issues that can arise
                      during the listener creation process.
                      When this parameter is set, AutoUpgrade uses a response file template to creates a response
                      file for the listener options that you specify in the target Oracle home. By default, this response
                      file is located at Oracle_home/assistants/netca/netca.rsp.

                      On Microsoft Windows platforms, the Oracle home is installed with secure user privileges, so
                      AutoUpgrade requires explicit authentication privileges to create the listener. Accordingly, if you
                      use this parameter, then you must modify the default netca.rsp file by updating the
                      SERVICEUSERPASSWORD parameter as follows:

                      1.    Remove the leading hash symbol (#).
                      2.    Replace the hash symbol with the actual password for the database installation owner user
                            account enclosed with quotes. For example:

                            SERVICEUSERPASSWORD="*******"

                      Syntax
                      create_lister[=default|my_listener:my_port|
                      listener_name1:listener_port1,listener_name2:listener_port2, . . .|/path/to/
                      responsefile.rsp]

                      Restrictions
                      •     You must specify listeners using alphanumeric characters for the name and numeric values
                            for the port.
                      •     If you use a path to a response file, then the response file target must be a valid response
                            file.

                      Examples
                      Create a listener with default values:

                      upg1.create_listener=default

drain_timeout
                      (Optional) Specifies the method that you want to use for draining the services before restarting
                      the instances while performing Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC) rolling patching.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      When you use AutoUpgrade to perform RAC rolling patching of Oracle RAC databases, you
                      can use this parameter in conjunction with the rac_rolling parameter to specify a time to wait
                      for sessions to drain on instances before shutting them down.

                      Syntax

                      upg.drain_timeout=value


                      Default: None.
                      Options:
                      •     value: Specify a non-negative integer limit for the maximum time, in seconds, that
                            AutoUpgrade waits for sessions to drain before stopping the instance. If the value is zero,
                            then instances are stopped immediately. If session draining completes in 10 seconds and
                            the drain timeout value is 100 seconds, then SRVCTL moves on after 10 seconds. It does
                            not wait for the remaining 90 seconds.
                      •     wait: Specifies that AutoUpgrade is to wait for all user sessions to drain from the instance
                            before stopping it.
                            AutoUpgrade first attempts a Transactional relocate of all services off the instance. If the
                            relocate operation fails, then AutoUpgrade falls back to a transactional stop of all services
                            on the instance. After draining completes, AutoUpgrade stops processing and waits for
                            input of a console command proceed -job #jobId, where jobId is the job that
                            AutoUpgrade paused as a result of drain_timeout=wait. When you enter proceed -job
                            #jobId, AutoUpgrade restarts the instance.

                      Restrictions
                      •     You cannot set this parameter if rac_rolling parameter=disabled.

                      Example
                      Suppose you set rac_rolling=required, and you want to specify that AutoUpgrade should set a
                      two-minute window for draining each instance before stopping them in the set of upgrades
                      specified with the prefix upg1. The AutoUpgrade parameters are as follows:
                      upg1.rac_rolling=required
                      upg1.drain_timeout=120

                      em_blackout_autoupgrade as follows:

                      (Required for AutoUpgrade patching, optional for Create Home and Deploy modes) Specifies

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option. This
                                parameter is for use with AutoUpgrade patching, and AutoUpgrade Create Home and
                                Deploy modes. Patching and upgrade operations are mutually incompatible. You can
                                either perform a patching operation, or a Create Home or Deploy mode operation, but
                                not both in the same configuration file.


                      The download_folder parameter (previously folder) indicates the directory location of
                      downloaded files. Starting with Oracle AI Database 26ai, you do not need to identify the base
                      image and store patch files in the same location. However, for releases earlier than Oracle AI
                      Database, for AutoUpgrade to perform patching, you must identify the directory that contains

                      conjunction with the download parameter as follows:
                      When download=YES, the directory specified by the download_folder parameter is the directory
                      to which the patches will be downloaded
                      When download=NO, the directory specified by the download_folder parameter is the directory
                      that must contain the patches that have been manually downloaded.
                      The directory that you specify with the download_folder parameter must contain the base
                      image of the source database's release (for example, Oracle Database Release 19.30).
                      When using AutoUpgrade in a patch operation, the folder you specify contains the patches to
                      perform maintenance on your database.
                      Starting with AutoUpgrade 25.6, you can also use the folder parameter in Create Home or
                      Deploy modes to specify a folder that contains a release update or patches that you want to
                      apply to database binaries in a target database release before starting an upgrade.

                      Examples

log_dir
                      (Optional) Sets the location of log files that are generated for database upgrades that are in the
                      set of databases included in the upgrade job identified by the prefix for the parameter.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      When set, AutoUpgrade creates a hierarchical directory based on a local log file path that you
                      specify. For example, where the job identifier prefix is sales, and where log_dir is identified
                      as upgrade-jobs, and stage1, stage2, and stagen represent stages of the upgrades:

                      /u01/app/oracle/upgrade-jobs
                                                                           /temp/
                                                                           /sales/
                                                                           /sales/stage1
                                                                           /sales/stage2
                                                                           /sales/stagen


                      You cannot use wild cards for paths, such as tilde (~). You must use a complete path.


                                Note
                                On Microsoft Windows platforms, global.autoupg_log and log_dir should be
                                configured on the same drive.


                      Example

                      salesdb.log_dir=/u01/app/oracle/upgrade-jobs


                      By default, if the global configuration file parameter global.autoupg_log_dir is specified, and
                      you do not specify log_dir, then the default is the path specified in global.autoupg_log_dir.

                      When neither global.autoupg_log_dir nor log_dir is specified, then by default the log files
                      are placed in the location indicated by the orabase utility for the databases that you include in
                      your configuration file. In that case, the default logs directory is in the path ORACLE_BASE/
                      cfgtoollogs/autoupgrade.

                      If the orabase utility fails for all databases included in the configuration file, then the log file
                      location is then based on the temp directory for the user running AutoUpgrade.

parallel_stats_degree
                      (Optional) Specifies the degree of parallelism to be used when gathering SYS and SYSTEM
                      dictionary statistics during the preupgrade fixup phase.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      ine option.
                      You can specify the degree of parallelism that AutoUpgrade uses when gathering statistics for
                      the SYS and SYSTEM dictionary schemas during the preupgrade phase. By default, if this
                      parameter is not set, then AutoUpgrade defaults to the standard database behavior, and
                      gathers statistics serially (default=no parallellism). You can use this parameter to increase the
                      number of parallel processes. Increasing the degree of parallelism can reduce the time
                      required to complete upgrade steps on large databases..
                      Default: None. If you do not specify this parameter, then AutoUpgrade uses the standard
                      database statistics gathering behavior and does not enforce a specific parallel degree.

                      Syntax

                      upg.parallel_stats_degree=value


                      The options for value are as follows:

                      •     Positive integer: Use the specified number of parallel threads for AutoUpgrade (for
                            example, 4 or 8).
                      •     0: Use the PL/SQL package DBMS_STATS.AUTO_DEGREE, which allows the database itself to
                            determine the optimal parallelism automatically, based on available resources. This option
                            is preferred when gathering statistics.

                      Restriction
                      You cannot set this parameter if the Common Locally Modifiable Global parameter
                      dictionary_stats_before is set to no (the default is yes).

                      Example
                      Set the degree of parallelism to 8 to gather SYS and SYSTEM dictionary statistics:

                      upg1.parallel_stats_degree=8


                      Specify that the database should automatically determine the optimal parallelism for gathering
                      SYS and SYSTEM dictionary statistics:

                      upg1.parallel_stats_degree=0

patch
                      (Required for AutoUpgrade patching, optional for AutoUpgrade Create Home and Deploy
                      modes) Specifies a comma-delimited list of the patches that you want to install.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option. This
                                parameter is for use with AutoUpgrade patching, and AutoUpgrade Create Home and
                                Deploy modes. Patching and upgrade operations are mutually incompatible. You can
                                either perform a patching operation, or a Create Home or Deploy mode operation, but
                                not both in the same configuration file.


                      Options

                      prefix.patch=option[,option,option...]


                      The default option value for patch is RECOMMENDED.

                      Options:
                      •     RECOMMENDED (Default): Alias for all of the following options: RU, OPATCH, OJVM, DPBP, AU.
                            Note that DBBP is not included with RECOMMENDED for Oracle Database 21c, OJVM is only
                            included for Oracle Database 19c, and that OCW is always included when the source is an
                            Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC) database.
                      •     AU: Download the latest version of AutoUpgrade.
                      •     AHF: Download the latest version of the Autonomous Heath Framework.
                      •     CSPU: Applies the latest Critical Security Patch Update for non-Linux systems. This option
                            is available for Oracle Database 19c and Oracle AI Database 26ai (applicable from 23.26
                            RU). It is not available for Oracle Database 21c.
                      •     CVU: Download the latest version of the Cluster Verification Utility
                      •     DPBP: Apply the Oracle Data Pump patch for the specified RU.
                      •     JDK: Apply the latest version of the Java Development Kit (JDK) patch.
                      •     GOLDIMAGE:gold_image_file.zip Identifies a gold image that can be used with -mode
                            create_home to use that specified gold image when creating the new target
                            ORACLE_HOME. This option does not support -mode download.
                      •     MRP: Apply the latest Monthly Recommended Patch (available for Linux only). This option is
                            available for Oracle Database 19c and Oracle AI Database 26ai (applicable from 23.26
                            RU). It is not available for Oracle Database 21c.
                      •     OCW[:x.y]: Apply the Oracle Clusterware patch of the specified release version, where x is
                            the major release number, and y is the RU. If the release version is unset, then

                            AutoUpgrade uses the RU version. In download mode, it will download the Grid
                            Infrastructure Release Update version x:y. For example: OCW:19.29.
                      •     OPATCH: Use latest version of OPatch.
                      •     OJVM[:x.y]: Apply the Oracle Java VM patch of the specified release version, where x is
                            the major release number, and y is the RU. If release version is unset, then AutoUpgrade
                            uses the RU version. For example: OJVM:19.24.
                      •     patch-number[,patch-number,patch-number...] specifies one or more specific one-off
                            patches that you want AutoUpgrade to apply, in order of priority.
                      •     RU[:x.y]: A release update (RU) of the specified release version, where x is the major
                            release number, and y is the RU. If the release number is unset, then AutoUpgrade will
                            take the latest release update. For example: RU:19.24
                      •     RECOMMENDED:x.y: Select the recommended patches for the specified RU version.
                      •     SDOBP: Apply the latest Oracle Spatial Bundle Patch.
                      •     SQLCL: Download the latest version of SQLcl
                      •     TEXT: Apply the latest Oracle TEXT patch for the specified RU. This option only applies for
                            an Oracle Database 19c Oracle home.
                      •     TOOLS: Download all tools (equivalent to AU, AHF, CVU and SQLCL).

                      Examples
                      patch-number: Provide a specific one-off patch number.

                      upg1.patch=ru:19.24,12345678,opatch


                      Apply recommended patches, which includes the set of recommended patch options: RU (the
                      latest release update for the specified target version), as well as OPATCH, OJVM, and DPBP:

                      upg1.patch=recommended


rac_rolling
                      (Optional) Specifies the RAC rolling patching policy for Oracle Real Application Clusters
                      (Oracle RAC) databases.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      Setting a RAC rolling policy for AutoUpgrade enables applying patch updates to Oracle RAC
                      databases without taking the entire cluster offline. Because at least part of the cluster remains
                      operational throughout the process, application downtime is avoided. AutoUpgrade performs
                      RAC rolling patching by restarting the instances one by one in new target home instead of
                      shutting down the entire database to avoid downtime while applying the patches.

                                                        Common Parameters for the AutoUpgrade Configuration File (Upgrade and Patch)



                      Options

                      [auto|required|disabled|force]


                      The default option value for patch is DISABLED.

                      Options:
                      •     AUTO: AutoUpgrade automatically determines whether it can perform Oracle RAC rolling
                            patching. If the precheck confirms eligibility, then AutoUpgrade attempts rolling patching.
                            Otherwise, it falls back to non-rolling patching. For Oracle RAC rolling patching, all patches
                            in the target Oracle home must support RAC rolling installation. Refer to each patch
                            README to confirm rolling support.
                      •     DISABLED: Always performs non-rolling patching (no Oracle RAC rolling updates).
                      •     FORCE: Specifies to attempt Oracle RAC rolling patching even if the precheck fails. Use this
                            option with caution, as this can affect availability if the environment is not rolling-ready.


                                     Note
                                     Effective only for patching operations in AutoUpgrade. Applies only to Oracle RAC
                                     databases. During Oracle RAC rolling patching, instances are patched one at a
                                     time to preserve service availability and avoid downtime.


                      •     REQUIRED: Specifies that performing Oracle RAC rolling patching is a required operation. If
                            the AutoUpgrade precheck stage fails to validate that the target home supports RAC rolling
                            patching, then the job stops with an error.

                      Example
                      AutoUpgrade performs RAC rolling patching and fails if the environment is not eligible.

                      upg1.rac_rolling=required


revert_after_action
                      (Optional) Specifies a custom action that you want to have run on the operating system after a
                      system restoration is completed for the specific database job addressed by the prefix, and the
                      database is up.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      The action that you specify with revert_after_action runs on the target Oracle home binaries
                      after the restoration process is completed, and the database is up.

                      The script that you specify to run must be in the form of name.ext (for example, myscript.sh),
                      so that AutoUpgrade can identify the type of script that you want to run. Permitted extension
                      options:
                      •     Unix shell (.sh)
                      •     Microsoft Windows batch (.bat, .cmd)
                      •     Microsoft Windows PowerShell (.ps1)
                      •     Oracle SQL script (.sql), with a local operation on the database designated by the
                            revert_before_action parameter prefix.

                      Options
                      Stop on fail: [Y|N]. The default is N.

                      By default, if the specified script fails, then AutoUpgrade continues to run (N. To specify that
                      AutoUpgrade stops if the script fails, use the Y flag. If the script finishes running on the
                      operating system with a status different than 0, then AutoUpgrade identifies the script as failed.

                      Examples
                      Run the script you specify on the operating system after AutoUpgrade completes processing
                      the restoration, with the Y flag set to stop AutoUpgrade if the script fails:

                      sales3.revert_after_action =/user/path/script.sh Y


                      Run the script you specify on the operating system after AutoUpgrade completes processing
                      the restoration. With no flag, the default stop on fail option is N, so AutoUpgrade continues to
                      run if the script fails:

                      sales3.revert_after_action =/user/path/script.sh


revert_before_action
                      (Optional) Specifies a custom action that you want to have run on the operating system before
                      a system restoration is completed for the specific database job addressed by the prefix, and
                      the database is up.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      The action that you specify with revert_before_action runs on the target Oracle home
                      binaries before database restoration is started, and the database is up.
                      The script that you specify to run must be in the form of name.ext (for example, myscript.sh),
                      so that AutoUpgrade can identify the type of script that you want to run. Permitted extension
                      options:
                      •     Unix shell (.sh)
                      •     Microsoft Windows batch (.bat, .cmd)

                      Options
                      Stop on fail: [Y|N]. The default is N.

run_utlrp
                      (Optional) Enables or disables running a version of utlrp.sql as part of post upgrade, to
                      recompile only invalid objects in Oracle-maintained schemas.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      The utlrp utility recompiles all Data Dictionary objects that become invalid during a database
                      upgrade. If you set run_utlrp=no, or if you want invalid user objects also to be recompiled,
                      then Oracle recommends that you use this utility to recompile invalid objects after upgrading
                      with AutoUpgrade.


                                Note
                                Starting with AutoUpgrade 23.1, when you run the AutoUpgrade utility, AutoUpgrade
                                runs the utlprpom.sql script, and does not run utlrp.sql. When AutoUpgrade is
                                used for upgrades to Oracle Database 18c (RU 18.8) and later releases, AutoUpgrade
                                only recompiles invalid objects owned by Oracle-maintained schemas. Because
                                database upgrades do not need to touch user objects, AutoUpgrade maintains this
                                policy when it recompiles invalid objects.

sid
                      (Required) Identifies the Oracle system identifier (SID) of the database that you want to
                      upgrade.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.

                                If the database is an Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC) database, then
                                you must specify the SID of the instance that runs on the server where you are
                                running AutoUpgrade.



                      This parameter is case-sensitive.

                      Example

                      sales1.sid=salesdb


source_home
                      (Required for analyze, fixups, and deploy modes. Optional for upgrade mode.) Current Oracle
                      home (ORACLE_HOME) of the database that you want to upgrade or patch.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      For the mode upgrade, the source home and target home values can be the same path.

                      Example

                      sales2.source_home=/path/to/my/source/oracle/home

start_time
                      (Optional) Sets a future start time for the upgrade or patching job to run. Use this parameter to
                      schedule jobs to balance the load on your server, and to prevent multiple jobs from starting
                      immediately.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.

                      Values must either take the form now (start immediately), or take the English Date Format form
                      DD/MM/YYYY or MM/DD/YYYY, where MM is month, DD is day, and YYYY is year. If you do
                      not set a value, then the default is now.

                      Permitted values:

                      now
                      30/12/2019 15:30:00
                      01/11/2020 01:30:15
                      2/5/2020 3:30:50


                      If more than one job is started with the start_time value set to now, then AutoUpgrade
                      schedules start times based on resources available in the system, which can result in start time
                      for jobs that are separated by a few minutes.
                      Values are invalid that use the wrong deliminator for the date or time element, or that use the
                      wrong date or hour format, such as the following:

                      30-12-2019 15:30:00
                      01/11/2020 3:30:15pm
                      2020/06/01 01:30:15


                      Examples

                      sales1.start_time=now
                      sales2.start_time=07/11/2020 01:30:15


Global Common Parameters for the AutoUpgrade Config File
                      The Common global parameters for the AutoUpgrade configuration file (config) enable you to
                      set a global parameter for both software maintenance (-patch) and upgrade (upgrade).

                      •     after_action
                            (Optional) Specifies a path and a file name for a custom user script that you want to have
                            run after all the upgrade jobs finish successfully.
                      •     autoupg_log_dir
                            (Deprecated) Sets the location of the log files, and temporary files that belong to global
                            modules, which AutoUpgrade uses.
                      •     before_action
                            (Optional) Specifies a custom user script that you want to have run for all upgrades before
                            starting the upgrade jobs.
                      •     global_log_dir
                            (Optional) Sets the location of the AutoUpgrade log files, and temporary files that belong to
                            global modules, which AutoUpgrade uses.
                      •     json_progress_writing_interval
                            (Optional) Sets the time interval for how often to write the AutoUpgrade progress JSON
                            report.
                      •     keystore

after_action
                      (Optional) Specifies a path and a file name for a custom user script that you want to have run
                      after all the upgrade jobs finish successfully.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      The script that you use must be in the form of name.ext (for example, myscript.sh, so that
                      AutoUpgrade can identify the type of script that you want to run. Permitted extension options:
                      •     Unix shell (.sh)
                      •     Microsoft Windows batch (.bat, .cmd)
                      •     Microsoft Windows PowerShell (.ps1)
                      By default, if the script fails, then AutoUpgrade continues to run. Use the Y flag to specify that
                      AutoUpgrade stops if the operating system detects that your script fails. If the script finishes
                      with a status different than 0, then it is considered a failed completion.

                      The output of the script is captured and stored in files. Both stdout and stderr are captured.
                      The files are stored in the postupgrade subdirectory in the directory matching the specific
                      database or job.
                      The following environment variables are set in the shell that runs the script:
                      •     ORACLE_SID
                      •     ORACLE_UNQNAME
                      •     ORACLE_BASE
                      •     ORACLE_HOME
                      •     TNS_ADMIN

                      Examples
                      If the script fails, then stop AutoUpgrade:

                      global.after_action=/path/to/my/script.sh Y


                      If the script fails, then continue AutoUpgrade:


                      global.after_action=/path/to/my/script.sh

autoupg_log_dir
                      (Deprecated) Sets the location of the log files, and temporary files that belong to global
                      modules, which AutoUpgrade uses.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      This parameters is now deprecated in favor of global_log_dir, which is now used with both
                      AutoUpgrade upgrades and patching.
                      You can configure different log directory path in the userconfig file in the logs directory for a
                      specific prefix
                      This parameter cannot be used with AutoUpgrade Patching.


                                Note
                                On Microsoft Windows platforms, global.autoupg_log and log_dir should be
                                configured on the same drive.


                      If you do not set this parameter to a path, then by default the log files are placed in the location
                      indicated by the orabase utility for the databases that you include in your configuration file. In
                      that case, the default logs directory is in the path ORACLE_BASE/cfgtoollogs/autoupgrade.

                      If the orabase utility fails for all databases included in the configuration file, then the log file
                      location is then based on the temp directory for the user running AutoUpgrade.

                      Examples

                      global.autoupg_log_dir=/path/to/my/global/log/dir


                      Configure different log directory path in the userconfig file in the logs directory for a specific
                      prefix

                      global.autoupg_log_dir=/path/to/my/global/log/dir
                      myprefix.log_dir=global.global_log_dir:different/path


                      The result of using this syntax is that log files and temporary files are placed in the following
                      path for databases identified by the prefix myprefix:

                      /path/to/my/global/log/dir/different/path

before_action
                      (Optional) Specifies a custom user script that you want to have run for all upgrades before
                      starting the upgrade jobs.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      The script that you use must be in the form of name.ext (for example, myscript.sh), so that
                      AutoUpgrade can identify the type of script that you want to run. If you want to have a script
                      run before a specific upgrade job, then specify that script by using the local parameter
                      (local.before_action)

                      Permitted extension options:
                      •     Unix shell (.sh)
                      •     Microsoft Windows batch (.bat, .cmd)
                      •     Microsoft Windows PowerShell (.ps1)
                      By default, if the script fails, then AutoUpgrade continues to run. Use the Y flag to specify that
                      AutoUpgrade stops if the operating system detects that your script fails. If the script finishes
                      with a status different than 0, then it is considered a failed completion.

                      The output of the script is captured and stored in files. Both stdout and stderr are captured.
                      The files are stored in the preupgrade subdirectory in the directory matching the specific
                      database or job.
                      The following environment variables are set in the shell that runs the script:
                      •     ORACLE_SID
                      •     ORACLE_UNQNAME
                      •     ORACLE_BASE
                      •     ORACLE_HOME
                      •     TNS_ADMIN

                      Examples
                      If the script fails, then stop AutoUpgrade:

                      global.before_action=/path/to/my/script.sh Y


                      If the script fails, then continue AutoUpgrade:


                      global.before_action=/path/to/my/script.sh

global_log_dir
                      (Optional) Sets the location of the AutoUpgrade log files, and temporary files that belong to
                      global modules, which AutoUpgrade uses.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      This configuration parameter is used for patching and upgrade. This parameter replaces
                      autoupg_log_dir parameter, which is deprecated. You can configure a different log directory
                      path in the userconfig file in the logs directory for a specific prefix.

                      If you do not set this parameter to a path, then by default the log files are placed in the location
                      indicated by the orabase utility for the databases that you include in your configuration file. In
                      that case, the default logs directory is in the path ORACLE_BASE/cfgtoollogs/
                      autoupgrade_patching.

                      If the orabase utility fails for all databases included in the configuration file, then the log file
                      location is then based on the temp directory for the user running AutoUpgrade.

                      Examples

                      global.global_log_dir=/path/to/my/global/log/dir


                      Configure different log directory path in the userconfig file in the logs directory for a specific
                      prefix

                      global.global_log_dir=/path/to/my/global/log/dir
                      myprefix.log_dir=global.global_log_dir:different/path


                      The result of using this syntax is that log files and temporary files are placed in the following
                      path for databases identified by the prefix myprefix:

                      /path/to/my/global/log/dir/different/path


                      The following is an example of a configuration file suing the global_log_dir parameter:

                      global.global_log_dir=/logs/patching
                      global.keystore=/secure/keystore
                      upg1.sid=DB19X
                      upg1.source_home=/databases/19x/dbhome_1
                      upg1.target_home=/databases/19x/dbhome_2
                      upg1.download_folder=/storage/patches
                      upg1.download=YES

json_progress_writing_interval
                      (Optional) Sets the time interval for how often to write the AutoUpgrade progress JSON report.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      This parameter specifies how often the AutoUpgrade progress JSON report is written. If you do
                      not set this parameter, then by default the AutoUpgrade progress JSON report interval is 30
                      seconds

                      Example
                      In the following example, global.json_progress_writing_interval=90 is used to specify that
                      the JSON progress report is written every 90 seconds to the log directory specified by
                      global.autoupg_log_dir:

                      global.json_progress_writing_interval=90
                      global.autoupg_log_dir=/path/to/my/global/log/dir


keystore
                      (Optional) Specifies the location for a dedicated software keystore used exclusively by
                      AutoUpgrade to store passwords, and other sensitive information.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                Common parameters work with or without the -patch command-line option.


                      You can use the keystore parameter to specify where you want AutoUpgrade to create a
                      dedicated software keystore that is used exclusively by AutoUpgrade.
                      The AutoUpgrade keystore contains the file ewallet.p12 (similar to other kind of keystores
                      used by the database). The file is created when you use the save command in the TDE
                      prompt. If you choose to generate an auto-login keystore, then the file cwallet.sso is created
                      as well. If you have an auto-login keystore, then AutoUpgrade does not prompt for a keystore
                      password when AutoUpgrade starts.
                      The keystore generated by AutoUpgrade contains sensitive information, and is protected by a
                      password that you choose when the keystore is used for the first time. Each time changes are
                      made to the keystore, the password must be supplied. Unless you decide to create an auto-
                      login keystore for AutoUpgrade, each time you start AutoUpgrade, and AutoUpgrade requires
                      information from the keystore, you must provide the keystore password.

                                Because the directory you specify with global.keystore contains a software keystore,

                      the keystore.

                      global.keystore=/etc/oracle/keystores/ORACLE_SID/autoupgrade



Upgrade Parameters for the AutoUpgrade Configuration File
                      The upgrade parameters for the AutoUpgrade configuration file (config) are used only with
                      upgrade operations.

                      •     Locally Modifiable Global Upgrade Parameters for the AutoUpgrade Configuration File
                            The Upgrade locally modifiable global parameters for the AutoUpgrade configuration file
                            enable you to set modifiable global parameters in the configuration (config) file that can be
                            overwritten by a database-specific local parameter.
                      •     Local Upgrade Parameters for the AutoUpgrade Config File
                            The upgrade local parameters enable you to configure AutoUpgrade processing in the
                            configuration file (config) for specific Oracle Databases for upgrades (upgrade).
                      •     Global Upgrade Parameters for the AutoUpgrade Config File
                            The upgrade global parameters for the AutoUpgrade configuration file (config) enable you
                            to set a global parameter for upgrades (upgrade).


Locally Modifiable Global Upgrade Parameters for the AutoUpgrade
Configuration File
                      The Upgrade locally modifiable global parameters for the AutoUpgrade configuration file
                      enable you to set modifiable global parameters in the configuration (config) file that can be
                      overwritten by a database-specific local parameter.
                      •     catctl_options
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Specifies one or more of a set of catctl.pl options
                            that you can select for AutoUpgrade to submit for catctl.pl to override default behavior.
                      •     defer_standby_log_shipping
                      •     drop_grp_after_upgrade
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Deletes the Guaranteed Restore Point (GRP) after
                            database upgrade.
                      •     enable_local_undo
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) For a CDB upgrade, specifies whether or not LOCAL

enable_local_undo
                      (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) For a CDB upgrade, specifies whether or not LOCAL undo
                      should be enabled before the upgrade of CDB$ROOT.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                For use with AutoUpgrade upgrades only. Patching and upgrade operations are
                                mutually incompatible. You can either perform a patching operation, or an upgrade
                                operation, but not both in the same configuration file.


                      If you select this option, then AutoUpgrade runs the following statement before upgrade: ALTER
                      DATABASE LOCAL UNDO ON;.

                      When local undo is first enabled, the size of the undo tablespace in PDB$SEED is determined as
                      a factor of the size of the undo tablespace in CDB$ROOT. The default is 30 percent of the undo
                      tablespace size. Every other PDB in the CDB inherits this property from PDB$SEED. Ensure that
                      there is enough space to allocate new UNDO tablespaces.

raise_compatible
                      (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Increases the Oracle Database COMPATIBLE initialization
                      parameter to the default value of the target release after the upgrade is completed
                      successfully.

                      Usage Notes
                      Options:
                      •     Y : Increase the COMPATIBLE parameter setting to the target release
                      •     N : Do not increase the COMPATIBLE parameter setting to the target release
                      •     Increase the COMPATIBLE level to a specific release update (RU) level (for example, 23.0,
                            23.4, 23.7)
                      The default is N.


                                Caution
                                •    After the COMPATIBLE parameter is increased, database downgrade is not possible.
                                •    Oracle recommends that you only raise the COMPATIBLE parameter to the current
                                     release level after you have thoroughly tested the upgraded database.
                                •    Regardless of what value you use for the autoupgrade command-line parameter
                                     restore, if you set the value of the configuration file parameter raise_compatible
                                     to yes, then before starting the upgrade, you must delete manually any
                                     guaranteed restore point you have created. After the upgrade is completed
                                     successfully, AutoUpgrade deletes the guaranteed restore point it creates before
                                     starting the upgrade. When AutoUpgrade starts the POSTUPGRADE stage, there
                                     is no way to restore the database.
                                •    If you specify to raise COMPATIBLE to a target RU level, then the the RU level you
                                     specify cannot be greater than the target Oracle home release. For example, if the
                                     target Oracle home release is updated to RU 23.4, then 23.7 is not a valid value
                                     for raise_compatible.



                      Examples
                      Raise COMPATIBLE to the level of the target Oracle Database home:

                      sales1.raise_compatible=yes

Local Upgrade Parameters for the AutoUpgrade Config File
                      The upgrade local parameters enable you to configure AutoUpgrade processing in the
                      configuration file (config) for specific Oracle Databases for upgrades (upgrade).

                      •     add_after_upgrade_pfile
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Specifies a path and file name of a PFILE whose
                            parameters you want to add after the upgrade.
                      •     add_during_upgrade_pfile
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Specifies a path and file name of a PFILE whose
                            parameters you want to add during the upgrade.
                      •     close_source
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Closes the source non-CDB or source PDB just
                            before AutoUpgrade starts a non-CDB to PDB conversion, starts an unplug-relocate
                            upgrade, or uses a refreshable clone PDB.
                      •     create_oracle_home
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Specifies whether to automatically create the target
                            oracle home in Deploy mode.
                      •     del_after_upgrade_pfile
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Specifies a path and file name of a PFILE whose
                            parameters you want to have removed after upgrade.
                      •     del_during_upgrade_pfile
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Specifies a path and file name of a PFILE whose
                            parameters you want to have removed during upgrade.
                      •     drop_dblink
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Specifies that the database link set up for an unplug-
                            plug relocate (hot clone) upgrade is dropped after successful job completion.
                      •     drop_win_src_service
                            (Optional for upgrades only) For upgrades on Microsoft Windows, specifies whether to
                            drop the Windows operating system service for the source Oracle Database after upgrade.
                      •     exclusion_list
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Sets a list of PDBs that you want to be excluded
                            from the AutoUpgrade run. This parameter only applies to the multitenant architecture
                            (CDB) databases. If you are plugging in and upgrading a non-CDB database, then this
                            parameter is ignored.
                      •     ignore_errors
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Enables you to specify a comma-delimited list of
                            specific Oracle errors that you want AutoUpgrade to ignore during the upgrade or patching
                            process.
                      •     keep_pdb_save_state
                            (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Specifies that if the PDB has a saved state in the
                            source CDB, then you can either save or not save the PDB state on the target CDB.

add_after_upgrade_pfile
                      (Optional for AutoUpgrade upgrades) Specifies a path and file name of a PFILE whose
                      parameters you want to add after the upgrade.

                      Usage Notes


                                Note
                                For use with AutoUpgrade upgrades only. Patching and upgrade operations are
                                mutually incompatible. You can either perform a patching operation, or an upgrade
                                operation, but not both in the same configuration file.


                      You can use the prefix to specify for which upgrade group you want to apply the PFILE
                      parameters.
                      In addition, within the PFILE that you specify with add_after_upgrade_pfile, you can specify
                      particular parameters for a specific named PDB. To specify parameters for a specific PDB, you
                      must enter the PDB-specific parameters using a comment line (#) in the PFILE. This
                      requirement is necessary so that AutoUpgrade can identify the parameters from the PFILE, but
                      the line otherwise ignored; for the database, PFILEs cannot contain PDB-specific parameter
                      values. For plug-in operations, use the original PDB or non-CDB name.
                      For specifying loading PFILE parameters for a named PDB, the following requirements apply
                      to the PFILE parameters:
                      •     The ispdb_modifiable column in V$SYSTEM_PARAMETER must be set to TRUE. If this value is
                            not set to TRUE, then the AutoUpgrade operation will fail.
                      •     If the issys_modifiable column in V$SYSTEM_PARAMETER is set to FALSE, then you must
                            restart the system so that the changes will be reflected in the PFILE. . Otherwise, changes
                            can be seen after the upgrade is complete.

                      Syntax

                      upgrade-batch].add_after_upgrade_pfile=value



Database Upgrade Guide
E96252-82                                                                                                      August 11, 2026
Copyright © 1996, 2026, Oracle and/or its affiliates.                                                          Page 112 of 245
                                                                                                                      Chapter 3
                                                                      Upgrade Parameters for the AutoUpgrade Configuration File


                      In a pfile, add a comment line specifying the PDB name and parameter, where the PDB name
                      is enclosed within brackets, and add the parameter name using the normal syntax for a
                      parameter in a PFILE:

                      [pdb-name].parameter-name=parameter-value


                      Examples
                      add_after_upgrade_pfile

                      sales3.add_after_upgrade_pfile=/path/to/my/pfile


                      To specify a particular parameter for a PDB, you first create your PFILE, and then edit the
                      PFILE to specify the PDB-specific parameters using comment lines. For example, suppose you
                      have a PDB named pdb10, and you want to specify the log archive destination
                      LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_4='LOCATION=/u02/oracle/oradata/payroll/' for pdb10, using the PFILE
                      sales3_params.ora as the basis for the parameters you want to apply. The procedure then is
                      as follows:
                      1.    Create a PFILE called pfile_add.ora with the initialization parameters you want to add
                            after upgrades with AutoUpgrade:

                            CREATE PFILE = 'pfile_add.ora' FROM SPFILE = 'sales3_params.ora';

                      2.    Open pfile_add_ora with a text editor such as vi, and add the line to specify the log
                            location as a comment line specified with the prefix # [pdb10], so that AutoUpgrade
                            identifies this as a parameter to add to the PFILE for pdb10:

                            *.local_listener='LISTENER_sales3'
                            *.nls_language='AMERICAN'
                            *.nls_territory='AMERICA'
                            *.sga_target=10641m
                            *.undo_tablespace='UNDOTBS1'
                            # [pdb10].LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_4='LOCATION=/u02/oracle/oradata/payroll/'

                      3.    Save pfile_add_ora in the location /u02/app/oracle/dbs.
                      4.    Open your configuration file and add the line ad_after_upgrade_pfile to specify the location
                            of pfile_add_ora:

                            sales3.add_after_upgrade_pfile=/u02/app/oracle/dbs/pfile_add.ora

                      5.    Run AutoUpgrade.
                      6.    After the upgrade is complete, the PFILE parameters from pfile_add.ora are applied to
                            the PDBs that are upgraded. In addition, for pdb10, this parameter is added to its PFILE:
                            LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_4=LOCATION=/u02/oracle/oradata/payroll/
                      7.    Shut down pdb10 and start it up again with the new PFILE parameter additions:

                            startup PFILE=$ORACLE_HOME/dbs/pdb10.ora
